title: Revision 11: Worked answer: innovation system, sustainable transformation, agency and institutions

chapters.title: Read the question
paragraphs: What do you understand by innovation system? What do you understand by sustainable transformation? What do you understand by agency? What do you understand by institutions?
The job of this part is to take that question apart before you write. Slides 34 and 35 of Class 9 ask for a direct definition, for how the readings and the classes use the term, and for one example.

There are four parts, and each part is its own term. The command is the same in each one. What do you understand by asks you to define the term, to show how the course uses it, and to give one example you can source. Those were the four parts.

Only Question 1 is compulsory. You then choose Question 2 or Question 3. The two answers are weighted equally, and no aids are allowed. Answers can be tested for plagiarism, so learn the moves and use your own words.
A weaker answer would write four dictionary lines and stop. A stronger answer would give each term a course definition, a name and a year, and one Norwegian case.
One way to say it: By this question, I understand four definitions, each with a source and a Norwegian example.
Remember: four terms, each defined, sourced and illustrated.

checks.q: What does what do you understand by ask for?
checks.a: A direct definition, how the course uses the term, and one example.

checks.q: How many terms does this question contain?

chapters.title: Innovation system
chapters.readings: Fagerberg et al. 2009, pp. 431, 434; Hekkert et al. 2007, pp. 416, 421, 426; Njøs et al. 2020, p. 273
paragraphs: The job of this part is the first definition. Slide 40 of Class 9 says to start from the readings and to clarify the concepts before you use them.

In plain words, an innovation system is how a place learns, not a single lab. More precisely, Fagerberg and colleagues, 2009, use a broad definition. It is all learning and innovation across an economy, not only in universities and laboratories. They trace the national form of that idea to Freeman, Lundvall and Nelson. The model answer narrows a national system to industries, a knowledge base and policies. Prefer the broad line. Those three parts are not the whole definition.

There is a second kind, and it does not replace the first. Hekkert and colleagues, 2007, citing Carlsson and Stankiewicz, describe a technological system as a network of agents that create, spread and use one technology under shared institutions. They study what those actors do, and they call those activities functions. There are seven, running from entrepreneurial activity through knowledge, guidance, markets, resources and legitimacy. One function affects the others, so the pattern is not a straight sequence.

The Norwegian case shows why the link matters. Njøs and colleagues, 2020, say maritime batteries in western Norway need both regional capabilities and demands that belong to the technology. Neither side alone explains the path. Fagerberg and colleagues add the national picture. Domestic suppliers in shipbuilding, engineering and services grew with petroleum, instead of Dutch disease.
One way to say it: By an innovation system, I understand learning across a whole economy, not only in universities and laboratories.
Remember: the broad definition comes first, and a technology system is a second kind, not a replacement.

checks.q: What is the broad definition, following Fagerberg and colleagues?
checks.a: All learning and innovation across an economy, not only universities and laboratories.

checks.q: What do maritime batteries need, according to Njøs and colleagues?
checks.a: Both regional capabilities and demands that belong to the technology.

chapters.title: Sustainable transformation
chapters.readings: Fløysand et al. 2022, p. 17; Schlaile et al. 2017, pp. 4, 5, 6; Class 9, slide 31; Class 2, slide 21
paragraphs: The job of this part is the second definition. Slides 34 and 35 of Class 9 still apply. Define the term as the course uses it, then show it in a case.

In plain words, the change has to point somewhere, or it is only novelty. More precisely, the exam-day sheet, taking the line from Fløysand and colleagues and citing UNEP, calls sustainable transformation change that cuts emissions and protects biodiversity. Their account of green industrial restructuring adds two further aims, less pollution and higher resource efficiency, such as a shift away from petroleum.

Schlaile and colleagues, 2017, keep the aim from becoming a slogan. A conventional path need not serve a social vision, so innovation is not sustainable on its own. They take the term dedicated innovation system from Pyka. It means a system pointed at transformations towards sustainability on purpose. Their three questions then ask what to sustain, who decides, and who answers.
The model answer reaches for a present-needs sentence and names Brundtland. Leave that as the definition. Slide 21 of Class 2 names the 1987 report in a policy line. It does not give you this term.
In Hordaland and Rogaland the work aims at a green shift, and yet oil and gas still dominates, unintentionally. That is the case. A shared aim is not the same as a finished transformation.
One way to say it: By sustainable transformation, I understand directed change that cuts emissions and protects biodiversity.
Remember: use the UNEP line, credit Pyka for the dedicated system, and do not define the term from the 1987 report.

checks.q: Which line should you use for sustainable transformation?
checks.a: Change that cuts emissions and protects biodiversity, from Fløysand and colleagues, citing UNEP.

checks.q: Where does the dedicated innovation system term come from?
checks.a: Schlaile and colleagues take it from Pyka.

chapters.title: Agency
paragraphs: The job of this part is the third definition. Slide 40 of Class 9 asks you to put the reading to use, not to list names. Revision six explains the agency range in full. Here you need the split this question asks for.

In plain words, agency is someone acting so that a path changes or stays. More precisely, Bækkelund, 2021, citing Sotarauta and Suvinen, treats agency as action that produces an effect, whether intended or not. Change agency alters a path, through entrepreneurship, institutional work or leadership. Reproductive agency keeps a path going. It can be resistance to what is new, and it is not only resistance. The reading does not call either kind sustainable or unsustainable.

Garud and Karnøe, 2003, add the picture you should refuse. Agency on a technology path is distributed across many actors. A single heroic inventor is the wrong picture. Their contrast, citing Levi-Strauss for the modest kind, is bricolage against a breakthrough attempt. Danish wind is read as bricolage. The United States path is read as the breakthrough attempt.

The villages show the split without leaving the reading. Flåm, Odda and Sogndal share institutions and the same surroundings, and they are tourism paths. Flåm shows more change agency than the other two. The same surroundings do not decide the outcome.
One way to say it: By agency, I understand work that can alter a path or keep it going, and that work is shared.
Remember: two kinds of agency, distributed across actors, and the villages are a tourism case.

checks.q: What is reproductive agency, following Bækkelund?
checks.a: The agency that keeps a path going, and it is not only resistance.

checks.q: Why is one heroic inventor the wrong picture?
checks.a: Because agency on a technology path is distributed across many actors.

chapters.title: Institutions
chapters.readings: Fagerberg et al. 2009, p. 433; Fløysand et al. 2022, pp. 15, 16, 22
paragraphs: The job of this part is the fourth definition. Slide 43 of Class 9 asks whether the readings are understood and fitted to the problem. A borrowed definition needs the name it is borrowed from.

In plain words, institutions are the rules people act inside. More precisely, Fagerberg and colleagues, 2009, citing North, call them the rules of the game. They are costly to establish, and once adopted they give scale. That is the line to learn. The model answer says the rules guide, legitimise and constrain behaviour. Prefer North's line, as the course states it.

Fløysand and colleagues, citing Lawrence and colleagues, then show the work actors do to those rules. Institutional work is physical and mental effort that can maintain, create, change or disrupt institutions. The same authors, citing Thornton and Almandoz, treat institutional logics as the patterns that make a practice look legitimate, and so shape what actors see as possible.

The two petroleum regions are the example. In diversified Hordaland, collective work legitimised a green shift. In petroleum-specialised Rogaland, individual work, tied to individual strategic leadership, delegitimised it. Both regions voiced a green shift. The work did not.
One way to say it: By institutions, I understand the rules of the game, costly to establish and then able to give scale.
Remember: North for the rules, Lawrence for the work on those rules, and the two regions for the contrast.

checks.q: How do Fagerberg and colleagues, citing North, define institutions?
checks.a: The rules of the game, costly to establish but scale-giving once adopted.

checks.q: What did the institutional work do in the two regions?
checks.a: It legitimised a green shift in Hordaland and delegitimised it in Rogaland.

chapters.title: How the four concepts connect
chapters.readings: Fagerberg et al. 2009, p. 431; Fløysand et al. 2022, p. 15; Bækkelund 2021, p. 758; Schlaile et al. 2017, p. 5; Class 9, slide 41
paragraphs: The job of this part is to join the four terms into one argument. Slide 41 of Class 9 says to sum up and to answer the question you were asked. You may return to a claim you made at the start.

There are four links, and each one stays inside a reading. First, the system is the learning across the economy. Fagerberg and colleagues, citing Arthur, add that history favours some solutions and holds others back. That is path dependency, and it is why a definition of the system needs its past. Second, sustainable transformation is the direction of that learning, not a reward you add at the end. Schlaile and colleagues say a conventional path need not serve a social vision. Third, agency is the work that can alter the path or keep it. Fourth, institutions are the rules that work maintains or rewrites. In the two regions, the same green aim met two kinds of institutional work, and the outcomes diverged.
A memory aid of our own: the learning, the aim, the work, then the rules.
A weaker answer would define the four terms in four sealed boxes. A stronger answer would show the work and the rules inside one system, aimed at one kind of change.
One way to say it: The system is the learning, the aim is the change, and actors and rules decide which path holds.
Remember: four terms, one argument, and the two regions are where they meet.

checks.q: What is path dependency, following Fagerberg and colleagues, citing Arthur?
checks.a: History that favours some solutions and holds others back.
The learning, the aim, the work, then the rules.

chapters.title: Traps and upgrades
chapters.readings: Fagerberg et al. 2009, pp. 431, 433; Schlaile et al. 2017, p. 4; Class 2, slide 21; Class 9, slide 43
paragraphs: The job of this part is to retire the lines that sound finished and are not what the course says. Slide 43 rewards readings that are understood, not a smoother story than the readings give you.
The first trap is the model answer's national system of industries, a knowledge base and policies. Instead, use the broad definition. It is learning across the whole economy.

The second trap is a present-needs sentence, with Brundtland as the source of sustainable transformation. Instead, use the UNEP line from Fløysand and colleagues. Slide 21 of Class 2 names the 1987 report in a policy line. It is not the definition.
The third trap is a dedicated innovation system with no origin. Instead, say that Schlaile and colleagues take the term from Pyka.
The fourth trap is to define institutions only as rules that guide, legitimise and constrain. Instead, citing North, call them the rules of the game, costly to establish and then able to give scale.

The fifth trap is a neat line that a university is an organisation and the rules around it are the institution. Instead, leave that line out. No course reading draws it. Flag it as outside the course.
Remember: prefer the corrected course line, and say so when a model answer goes past it.

checks.q: What should you say instead of the three-part national system?
checks.a: Learning across the whole economy, following Fagerberg and colleagues.

checks.q: What should you do with the organisation versus institution line?
checks.a: Leave it out. No course reading draws it.

chapters.title: Build it yourself
chapters.readings: Fagerberg et al. 2009, pp. 431, 433; Fløysand et al. 2022, p. 17; Bækkelund 2021, p. 758; Schlaile et al. 2017, p. 4
paragraphs: The job of this part is to make you say the four definitions without the script. Pause after each question. Then check yourself.
Give the broad definition of an innovation system. Pause the audio and answer in your head.
Here is the answer. By an innovation system, I understand learning across a whole economy, not only in universities and laboratories. Fagerberg and colleagues, 2009, give that broad line.
Give the course line for sustainable transformation. Pause the audio and answer in your head.

Here is the answer. By sustainable transformation, I understand change that cuts emissions and protects biodiversity. The line comes from Fløysand and colleagues, citing UNEP. A dedicated system, the term Schlaile and colleagues take from Pyka, points that change on purpose.
Separate change agency from reproductive agency. Pause the audio and answer in your head.
Here is the answer. By agency, I understand work that can alter a path or keep it going. Bækkelund, 2021, separates change agency from reproductive agency. The work is shared across actors.
Give the course line for institutions. Pause the audio and answer in your head.
Here is the answer. By institutions, I understand the rules of the game. Fagerberg and colleagues, citing North, say those rules are costly to establish and then able to give scale.
Say your whole plan aloud in under one minute. Pause the audio and answer in your head.

Here is the answer. By an innovation system, I understand learning across a whole economy, not only in universities and laboratories. By sustainable transformation, I understand change that cuts emissions and protects biodiversity. By agency, I understand work that can alter a path or keep it going, and that work is shared. By institutions, I understand the rules of the game, costly to establish and then able to give scale.
Remember: the four openers are the part to know by heart.

checks.q: How many openers does the last answer repeat?
Whose name belongs with the rules of the game?
checks.a: North, as cited by Fagerberg and colleagues.
